# Qusetion 1

## Load dataset
```{r}
# install.packages("fpp2")

library(fpp2)
str(euretail)
```
The database presents the Quarterly Index of Retail Trade in the Eurozone (17 countries), over the period 1996-2012. It is a time series of 64 observations.

## Plot a data
```{r}
autoplot(euretail, main="Data") + ylab("Retail index") + xlab("Year")
```

Since the time series has a non-stationary variance, it would be interesting to perform a logarithmic or Box-Cox transformation on the data. As for the stationarity, the graph suggests that the series is not stationary. We will have more precision by performing an augmented Dickey-Fuller test.

## Stationarity check
```{r}
#install.packages("tseries")

library(tseries)

adf.test(euretail)
```

With an alpha of 0.05 and p-value of 0.99, we fail to reject the null ans stat that the series is not stationary.

## Forecasting

```{r}
fit<-auto.arima(euretail)
summary(fit)
```
The model obtained has an RMSE of 0.36 on the basis of training data. It has seasonal components, Differencing I(1) and Moving average MA(3) in addition to non-seasonal components, I(1) and MA(1) with the seasonal period is S = 4


## Plot ACF and PACF of residuals
```{r}
euretail %>%
  auto.arima() %>%
  residuals() %>% 
  ggtsdisplay()
```

All peaks in the ACF and PACF plots are within significance, so the residuals appear to be white noise, which is a good result.

## Check residuals
```{r}
checkresiduals(fit)
```
The Ljung-Box test shows that the residuals are not autocorrelated and the distribution graph makes us think of a normal distribution of the residuals. We can therefore conclude that the residuals are random.

# Question 2

## Load dataset and display April 1st, 2022 COVID data
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(xts)
df <- read_excel("COVID_Cases_Deaths - 2023.xlsx")
df$date <- as.Date(df$date)
df_ts<-xts(df$deaths, df$date)
print(df_ts["2022-04-01"])
```
## Plot a data
```{r}
autoplot(df_ts)
```

The data are non-stationary, with non-constant variance and mean, with a rising trend.

## Stationarity check
```{r}
adf.test(df_ts)
```
With an alpha of 0.05 and p-value of 0.388, we fail to reject the null ans stat that the series is not stationary.

## Forecasting
```{r}
fit<-auto.arima(df_ts)
summary(fit)
```
The model obtained has an RMSE of 746.1825 on the basis of training data. It has seasonal components, Differencing I(1)  with drift and nothing non-seasonal components.

## Plot ACF and PACF of residuals
```{r}
df_ts %>%
  auto.arima() %>%
  residuals() %>% 
  ggtsdisplay()
```

The ACF and PACF plots show several significant and nearly significant peaks. indicating that some additional non-seasonal terms should be included in the model.

## Check residuals
```{r}
checkresiduals(fit)
```

The Ljung-Box test shows that the residues are autocorrelated.

## Repeat previous step for only 2023 COVID data

### Plot a data
```{r}
autoplot(df_ts["2023"])
```

The data are non-stationary, with non-constant variance and mean, with a rising trend.

### Stationarity check
```{r}
adf.test(df_ts["2023"])
```
With an alpha of 0.05 and p-value of 0.9816, we fail to reject the null ans stat that the series is not stationary.

### Forecasting
```{r}
fit<-auto.arima(df_ts["2023"])
summary(fit)
```
The model obtained has an RMSE of 452.9056 on the basis of training data. It has seasonal components, Differencing I(1) and Moving average MA(1) with drift and nothing non-seasonal components.

### Plot ACF and PACF of residuals
```{r}
df_ts["2023"] %>%
  auto.arima() %>%
  residuals() %>% 
  ggtsdisplay()
```

The ACF and PACF plots show significant peaks at lag 4,7,16 and almost significant at lag 3,6. indicating that some additional non-seasonal terms should be included in the model.

## Check residuals
```{r}
checkresiduals(fit)
```

The Ljung-Box test shows that the residues are autocorrelated.While the distribution of residuals appears to be normal.
